Warlock · Theorycraft

Maximum Dominance Warlock

single-stat walling caster

Warlock theorycraft unchanged single-stat walling caster confidence medium

Last verified 2026-08-09 • Season 14

Untested theorycraft; no source publishes this build. 3.1.0 changed Wall of Agony so that it scales off Maximum Dominance, and doubled its Encircle upgrade's per-demon damage reduction from 3% to 6%. The class already has a dedicated Dominance generator in Mastermind Shard's Subjugation Fragment, which produces 2 Dominance per second. Put those together and Maximum Dominance became the rare thing in this game: one stat that is simultaneously the offensive scalar and the defensive one, so every point of it is paid for twice. This build asks whether that is enough to carry a character. It is worth being blunt about the class context. Warlock is last on the 3.1.2 class snapshot, has no build above B on Maxroll's endgame list, and its published builds are Apocalypse and the Lunatic shell - not this. The one dissenting voice is InfinityBuilds' 2026-08-02 list, which puts a Command Fallen Warlock in S, and it is not dissenting about Wall of Agony.

Requirements

  • Fleshwrit Carapacechest
  • Moloch's Beating Flameamulet
  • Hands of the Worldbreakergloves
Stage
Move on whenLevel 70, Torment 1, and Maximum Dominance high enough that Wall of Agony's damage is visibly scaling with it rather than sitting flat.
Move on whenBoth measurements taken. If Encircle counts only its own demons, the defensive half of the hypothesis is much weaker than this page assumes and the build should be re-judged on damage alone.
Move on whenThe comparison is done and this build won on at least one axis. Warlock is the weakest class in this season's data; a variant that loses on both axes has no reason to exist.

Rotation

Command Fallen to get demons out, Umbral Chains to pull the pack in, Wall of Agony to encircle it. Dread Claws and Bombardment while the wall does its work. The thing to watch at this stage is simply whether Maximum Dominance is a number you can move: if the gear cannot produce a meaningful total, nothing downstream is worth testing.

How to run them

Carried over from the class's published build rather than derived from this hypothesis. Raheir hired for the cheat-death and Aldkin reinforcing, which is the pairing the Apocalypse guide's planner records. A build whose defensive layer ramps with demon count has a window at the start of every fight where it has no defensive layer at all, so a cheat-death is at least the right shape of answer - but that is reasoning, not testing. The tree picks are the published Apocalypse build's, inherited node for node; Raheir's four are the same four whichever Warlock hires him.

Reasoning

HypothesisMaximum Dominance is now a dual-purpose stat for Warlock and nothing is built around it. 3.1.0 made Wall of Agony scale off Maximum Dominance and took its Encircle upgrade's per-demon damage reduction from 3% to 6%, while Mastermind Shard's Subjugation Fragment generates 2 Dominance per second. If Maximum Dominance can be stacked hard enough on gear, a single stat drives both a damage skill and a stacking damage-reduction layer that scales with the demon count the class produces anyway - which is a fundamentally more efficient use of an affix budget than the meta build's three separate scaling layers (Fire and Hellfire multipliers, an Overpower package, and a charm set).
Confidencemedium
How to test it(1) The first question is whether Maximum Dominance is actually stackable to an interesting number on gear. The knowledge base records that Wall of Agony scales off it and that the Subjugation Fragment generates 2 per second; it does not record how much Maximum Dominance a finished character can reach, and that number decides whether this is a build or a curiosity. Read it off the character sheet with the Dominance affixes on every slot that can roll them. (2) Confirm that Encircle's per-demon damage reduction counts every demon the class can have out, not only demons Wall of Agony itself created - the wording in the patch notes is per-demon and does not say. This is the difference between a strong defensive layer and a marginal one. (3) Measure Wall of Agony's actual damage against Bombardment and Command Fallen on the same character. Wall of Agony has always been a control skill; making it scale off a stat does not automatically make it a damage skill. (4) Check the interaction between the Dominance pool and the Wrath pool, since the class runs two resources and a build that spends only one of them is wasting half its resource generation. (5) Compare to warlock-meta-apocalypse on a Pit floor; if this build cannot match it, say so and stop - Warlock's floor is low enough already without a worse build on top of it.
